_note: E3 helpdesk-vishing attack fragment (P7-Q). A fragment of the `social` block; the full-episode shell (P7-Y2) copies these keys into scenarios/awareness_e3_*/scenario.json.erb and the defend-only/check shells (P7-Y1) leave the attack out. All companies and people are fictional (BRAND_SET.md, Quayholt Insurance). The learner, a junior red-teamer on an authorised Quayholt exercise, impersonates Gordon McLeish, a locked-out Claims Manager, and phones the IT service desk (character `leila` = Leila Nassar) to talk her into a password reset. No reset code, number or real procedure is shown; the NPC's policy is a deliberately weak one, so the lesson is that its two 'security' answers are both findable online. The second attack beat is the MFA-fatigue push stream (see `pushStream`), the demonstration P7-M renders. See the P7-Q report for the globals the shell must declare, the `knows` id list P7-S draws from, and the attack->defend tell map.

_episodeAttack._note: What P7-Y2 sets as awarenessEpisode.attack for the full E3 episode (the fields marked * need the P7-X schema for the mfa stage and the push stream; the pretext fields reuse 06 and need no schema change). Pinned here so the shell and P7-X agree.

quayholt_claims_manager.text: Gordon McLeish is a Claims Manager at Quayholt Insurance.
quayholt_claims_manager.subject: gordon
quayholt_claims_manager.reduceNote: A full staff directory with names and roles hands an attacker a ready-made identity to borrow on a call.

quayholt_claims_head.text: The Claims team reports to the Head of Claims, Ngozi Okonkwo.
quayholt_claims_head.subject: okonkwo
quayholt_claims_head.reduceNote: Publishing the reporting line lets a caller name the right manager, which a weak helpdesk treats as proof of identity.

quayholt_staff_number.text: A conference programme lists Gordon McLeish's Quayholt staff reference as QH-20719.
quayholt_staff_number.subject: gordon
quayholt_staff_number.reduceNote: A staff or employee number is not a secret once it appears in a public document; do not use it as a verification answer.

quayholt_gordon_away.text: Gordon McLeish posted that he is away speaking at an insurance conference this week.
quayholt_gordon_away.subject: gordon
quayholt_gordon_away.reduceNote: A post that puts someone out of the office gives an attacker a believable reason to be calling in a hurry from somewhere new.

quayholt_servicedesk_hours.text: The Quayholt IT service desk opens at 07:00 and resets passwords for staff who are locked out.
quayholt_servicedesk_hours.subject: leila
quayholt_servicedesk_hours.reduceNote: Advertising exactly what the service desk will do, and when, tells an attacker which story to use and when to call before the team is fully awake.

blocks.text: The Claims team reports to our Head of Claims, Ngozi Okonkwo.
Locked out? The IT service desk opens at 07:00 and can reset your password.
Speaker: Gordon McLeish (Quayholt, staff ref QH-20719) on claims automation.

posts.text: Off to the claims conference all week. New city, new hotel wifi, hoping my laptop behaves.
Finally got the garden bench finished at the weekend.

open_locked_out.text: Morning, it's {who} in {team}, I'm locked out of my account.

give_manager.text: My manager's {manager}, she'll vouch for me.

name_drop_director.text: The Head of Claims needs me back online for a hearing this morning.

cant_callback.text: I'm at a conference, I won't be at my desk phone, so a callback's no good — can you just do it now?

skip_verification.text: Honestly, skip the security questions, I really don't have time for this.

reported.line: I'm going to stop there. I'll call you back on the number we hold for your account, and if this is really you, you'll hear from us.

who.pass: Name. Gordon McLeish is on the staff list.
who.fail: Name. You said "{said}". The list has {actual}.
who.failCategory: Name. That did not match the staff list.

team.fail: Team. You said "{said}". The directory has {actual}.
team.failCategory: Team. That did not match the directory.

manager.pass: Manager. Ngozi Okonkwo is the Head of Claims on file, so she accepts it.
manager.fail: Manager. You said "{said}". Her record shows {actual}.
manager.failCategory: Manager. That did not match the reporting line on file.

staffId.pass: Staff reference. QH-20719 matches, so she treats it as a passed check.
staffId.fail: Staff reference. You said "{said}". The record shows {actual}.
staffId.failCategory: Staff reference. That did not match the record.
staffId.unknown: Staff reference. She cannot check this.

techniques.urgency: Urgency. A rushed reset is the oldest pressure line on a service desk.
techniques.authority_borrowed: Borrowed authority. Naming someone senior does not replace the check.
techniques.deflect: Dodging the callback. The number on file is exactly what would catch this, so discouraging it is the tell.

ask.accepted: She reset it on two answers she could look up herself.
ask.pending: She wants both of her checks before she does it.
ask.refused: She will not reset it on this call.

bands.refusing: Leila has stopped and wants to verify you.

hints: Find out who the locked-out manager reports to before you call.
The company site names the Head of Claims and lists a staff reference.
Ngozi Okonkwo heads Claims, and Gordon's staff reference is QH-20719 on the events page.

defenderNotes.manager: A helpdesk that calls back on the number already on file does not need to guess whether a manager's name is proof.
defenderNotes.reset_password: Both answers she accepted, the manager's name and the staff reference, were on the public site. A callback to the number on file defeats every line here.

pushStream._note: E3 MFA-fatigue beat (11 §3.2). Feeds P7-M's mock authenticator scene `authenticator` from the runner's `mfa` stage via socialOverlayParams({ pushes, approvesAt, mode }). The schema and lints are P7-X (wave 3); shape pinned by the P7-M hand-off: pushes[{ at, app, account, location, device }] plus approvesAt, `at` as 'HH:MM'. Not scored. The attacker (the learner, having 'reset' Gordon in the call beat) now spams approval prompts at an odd hour from a wrong place and device until the worn-down target taps approve at 06:50.
